chapterName: Empire: Augustus and the Principate (27 BC-AD 14)

questions.question: What did Octavian's propaganda accuse Mark Antony of? (select all that apply)
options: Abandoning his Roman wife, Octavian's sister
Plotting the murder of Julius Caesar
Giving Roman lands to the queen's children
questions.explanation: Octavian accused Antony of leaving Octavian's own sister for a foreign queen and giving away Roman lands to her children. In 32 BC the Senate declared war on Cleopatra.
questions.sourceQuote: Octavian waged a fierce propaganda war, accusing Antony of abandoning his Roman wife, Octavian's own sister, for a foreign queen and of giving away Roman lands to her children.

questions.question: How did the conflict with the queen of Kush on Egypt's southern border end?
options: A treaty fixed a new border and guaranteed trade
Kush was annexed as a Roman province
The queen was taken to Rome in chains
questions.explanation: After her raids and Roman counterattacks, the queen sent envoys and a treaty followed. Kush was a kingdom in modern Sudan.
questions.sourceQuote: After Roman counterattacks she sent envoys, and a treaty fixed a new border and guaranteed trade.

questions.question: How did Augustus recover the legionary standards held by the Parthians in 20 BC?
questions.explanation: Some Romans wanted revenge, but Augustus presented the deal as Parthia bowing to Rome. The standards were housed in the Temple of Mars the Avenger.
questions.sourceQuote: In 20 BC Augustus negotiated their return without a fight.

questions.question: Why was the proposal to name Octavian after Romulus rejected?
questions.explanation: Romulus was Rome's legendary founder and first king, and Romans hated the idea of a king. The Senate chose Augustus instead.
questions.sourceQuote: Another suggestion, to call him after Romulus, Rome's legendary founder and first king, was rejected as too royal.

questions.question: What claim about Augustus's death do many modern historians dismiss as slander?
options: That he died in battle in Germany
That he took his own life
That his wife poisoned him, perhaps with a fig
questions.explanation: Two ancient historians made the poisoning claim. Augustus died at Nola, near Naples, on 19 August AD 14, aged 75.
questions.sourceQuote: Two ancient historians claimed his wife, Livia, poisoned him, perhaps with a fig, but many modern historians dismiss this as slander.

questions.question: What was the first act of the triumvirate formed by Octavian, Mark Antony and a third general?
options: A purge of senators and wealthy businessmen
A grain dole for the poor
questions.explanation: About 300 senators and wealthy businessmen were declared outlaws, and thousands more lost their property.
questions.sourceQuote: About 300 senators and wealthy businessmen were declared outlaws, and thousands more lost their property.

questions.question: What did the mock naval battle Augustus staged in 2 BC recreate?
options: A Greek sea victory over Persia
Agrippa's defeat of a renegade admiral
questions.explanation: The battle was fought on an artificial lake fed by a new aqueduct more than 30 km long. Rome's first stone amphitheatre also opened in his time.
questions.sourceQuote: Rome's first stone amphitheatre opened in his time, and in 2 BC he staged a mock naval battle on an artificial lake fed by a new aqueduct more than 30 km (twenty miles) long, recreating a famous Greek sea victory over Persia.

questions.question: How did Augustus reportedly react to news of the Varian Disaster?
options: He banged his head on the palace walls
questions.explanation: It was said he cried for the dead commander to give him back his legions. Rome then abandoned conquest beyond the Rhine.
questions.sourceQuote: Augustus, it was said, banged his head against the palace walls, crying for the dead commander to give him back his legions.

questions.question: Why did Augustus avoid openly naming an heir?
options: He hoped to restore the Republic
It would look like founding a monarchy
questions.explanation: Augustus had no son, so he quietly promoted relatives instead.
questions.sourceQuote: Augustus had no son, and naming an heir openly would have looked like founding a monarchy.

questions.question: Why had holding the consulship every year become a problem for Augustus by 23 BC?
options: It required him to lead armies abroad
It made his dominance obvious and blocked rivals
It cost him his private fortune
It was banned by an old law
It forced him to live outside Rome
questions.explanation: Being elected consul every year made his dominance plain and shut out other ambitious senators. He gave it up on 1 July 23 BC.
questions.sourceQuote: Augustus had been elected consul every year, which made his dominance obvious and blocked other ambitious senators.
